findings.title: Backup codes cannot be used by Google/SAML users with 2FA, locking them out
findings.body: In the credentials authorize callback, the guard `if (user.identityProvider !== IdentityProvider.CAL && !credentials.totpCode) throw new Error(ErrorCode.ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled)` runs before the new backup-code branch. Users who log in via Google/SAML and have 2FA enabled go through the totp JWT flow (`loginWithTotp`), which submits no totpCode and no password — so if they lose their authenticator and try a backup code, they get 'third-party-identity-provider-enabled' instead of the backup-code check. Backup codes are precisely the recovery mechanism for lost authenticator access, so these users have no recovery path at all. The IdP checks should be skipped when a valid backupCode is supplied (the backup code itself is the second factor).

findings.title: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write, allowing code reuse under concurrency
findings.body: The code decrypts the backup code list, checks `indexOf`, sets `backupCodes[index] = null`, and re-encrypts in a separate update. Two concurrent login requests presenting the same backup code can both read the list before either writes, both pass the `indexOf` check, and both be authenticated — defeating the single-use guarantee of backup codes (which the UI copy explicitly promises: 'Each backup code can be used exactly once'). The check-and-consume should be made atomic (e.g., a transaction with a conditional update, or a per-code row with a unique consumed marker).

findings.title: Consumed backup codes become permanent null entries; once all 10 are used there is no recovery or regeneration path
findings.body: Used codes are replaced with `null` inside the stored array rather than removed, and there is no endpoint or UI to regenerate backup codes. After all 10 codes are consumed, `user.backupCodes` is still non-null, so the 'MissingBackupCodes' branch never triggers; the user just gets 'incorrect-backup-code' forever. The new locale string 'missing_backup_codes' tells users to 'generate them in your settings', but no such settings UI exists in this PR, so the message directs users to a non-existent feature. Either add a regeneration flow (e.g., rerun setup) or fix the message and prune null entries.

findings.title: Dismissing the dialog after enabling 2FA (Esc/overlay click) skips onEnable and leaves stale state
findings.body: After `handleEnable` succeeds, the modal moves to the DisplayBackupCodes step, and `onEnable()` (which notifies the parent that 2FA is now enabled, updating the settings switch) is only called from the explicit 'Close' button. If the user dismisses the dialog via Escape or clicking the overlay, `onOpenChange` fires, `onEnable` is never called, and `resetState` is never run — the parent UI still shows 2FA as disabled even though it is enabled in the database, and reopening the modal resumes at the stale DisplayBackupCodes step. Handle cleanup in `onOpenChange` (or a useEffect on `open`) so enable notification and state reset happen on any close path.

findings.title: No tests cover the core new behavior: logging in with a backup code or disabling 2FA with one
findings.body: The PR's main feature is using backup codes during the 2FA login flow and in the disable-2FA flow, but the only test additions exercise the setup screen's copy/download/close buttons, and the file itself adds a TODO admitting login-with-backup and disable-with-backup tests are missing. The single-use consumption logic in the credentials provider, the dash-stripping (`replaceAll('-', '')`), and the new error paths (IncorrectBackupCode, MissingBackupCodes) are entirely untested. The PR checklist also states no tests were added proving the feature works. At minimum, an e2e test should log in with a backup code and verify the same code is rejected on a second attempt.

findings.title: Backup code minLength/maxLength rely on native validation that is disabled on the login form
findings.body: The input enforces the code length via native `minLength={10}`/`maxLength={11}` attributes, but the login form in `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx` renders with `noValidate`, so these constraints are never enforced there; any-length string is submitted as `backupCode`. Additionally the placeholder/format 'XXXXX-XXXXX' is 11 characters with the dash, so a correctly formatted code sits at the maxLength boundary and the 10-char minimum rejects a valid 10-char code entered without the dash. Move length/format validation into the zod schema or the server (the server already strips dashes, so client-side length constraints are redundant and currently misleading).
